# Fix it yourself

Every fix VTDiag can propose, done by hand. VTDiag v0.1 only scans; use these steps for the fixes your report lists. Change one thing at a time and play a match before the next one.

<!-- This file is generated by `tools/kb_builder.py` from `tools/kb_curation/manual_steps.py`. Do not edit it by hand. -->

## Stop your Bluetooth headset from switching to 'phone call' mode

`fix.audio.bt_handsfree_off`

When VALORANT voice chat opens your Bluetooth headset's microphone, Windows switches the headset to Hands-Free mode, which sounds like an old phone call. We'll switch off Hands-Free mode, so game sound stays clear.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Device Manager".
2. Open "Sound, video and game controllers" and find each Hands-Free device VTDiag named in your report.
3. Right-click it and choose "Disable device", then click "Yes".
4. Do the same for every Hands-Free entry in the report, then reconnect your headset.
5. To undo, right-click the same device and choose "Enable device".

**Undo:** Press Undo and Hands-Free mode comes back.

## Turn off fullscreen optimizations for VALORANT

`fix.display.disable_fso`

Windows 'fullscreen optimizations' change how the game is shown on screen. For some players this causes stutter or alt-tab freezes. We'll switch them off for VALORANT only.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Close VALORANT and the Riot Client.
2. Open the folder of the VALORANT file VTDiag named in your report (VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe).
3. Right-click that file and choose "Properties", then open the "Compatibility" tab.
4. Tick "Disable fullscreen optimizations" and click "OK" (do not use "Change settings for all users").
5. Start VALORANT and play one match to check.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the setting is removed.

## Turn off Xbox Game Bar background recording

`fix.display.game_dvr_off`

Game Bar can record your gameplay in the background all the time. That recording costs FPS and can cause stutter. We'll switch off background recording (Game Bar itself stays).

1. Press Win+R, type "regedit" and press Enter to open Registry Editor.
2. Go to the key "HKEY_CURRENT_USER\System\GameConfigStore", right-click it and choose "Export" to save a backup.
3. Double-click "GameDVR_Enabled", set "Value data" to 0 and click "OK".
4. Go to "HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\GameDVR" and export it as a backup too.
5. Double-click "AppCaptureEnabled" (or create it with New > DWORD (32-bit) Value), set it to 0 and click "OK".
6. Sign out and back in, then play one match; to undo, double-click your saved backup files.

**Undo:** Press Undo and background recording comes back.

## Run VALORANT on your graphics card

`fix.display.gpu_pref_high`

Your PC has two graphics chips, and Windows may run VALORANT on the weaker built-in one. We'll tell Windows to always use the strong graphics card for VALORANT.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Open Settings > System > Display > Graphics (on Windows 10 the link is called "Graphics settings").
2. Click "Browse" and pick the VALORANT file VTDiag named in your report, or click it if it is already in the list.
3. Click the app, then "Options".
4. Choose "High performance" and click "Save".
5. Restart VALORANT so it starts on your graphics card.

**Undo:** Press Undo and Windows chooses by itself again.

## Turn off hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling

`fix.display.hags_off`

Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (HAGS) is a Windows graphics option. With some drivers it causes stutter, input delay or freezes in VALORANT. We'll switch it off. It takes effect after a restart.

**Admin rights needed** · **Restart needed**

1. Open Settings > System > Display > Graphics.
2. On Windows 11, click "Change default graphics settings"; on Windows 10 the option is right on the "Graphics settings" page.
3. Turn "Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling" off.
4. Restart the PC, then play one match.

**Undo:** Press Undo and restart to switch it back on.

## Turn off Multi-Plane Overlay (MPO)

`fix.display.mpo_off`

Multi-Plane Overlay is a Windows display feature that some graphics drivers handle badly, causing flicker, alt-tab freezes or micro-stutter. We'll switch it off with the same setting NVIDIA recommends.

**Admin rights needed** · **Restart needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "regedit" and press Enter to open Registry Editor.
2. Go to the key "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Dwm", right-click it and choose "Export" to save a backup.
3. Right-click the empty right side and choose New > DWORD (32-bit) Value, and name it "OverlayTestMode" (skip this if it already exists).
4. Double-click "OverlayTestMode", set "Value data" to 5 and click "OK".
5. Restart the PC; to undo, double-click your saved backup file and restart.

**Undo:** Press Undo and restart to switch it back on.

## Close this program for this session

`fix.generic.close_process`

This program is known to clash with VALORANT. We'll ask it to close (like clicking its X). It starts again next time you turn on your PC.

1. Find the program VTDiag named in your report.
2. Close its window with the X button.
3. If it still runs near the clock, right-click its tray icon and choose "Exit" or "Quit".
4. It will start again next time you turn on your PC, so repeat this before you play if needed.

**Undo:** Nothing to undo: open the program again whenever you want.

## Turn off this device

`fix.generic.disable_device`

This device or its driver is known to clash with VALORANT. We'll switch it off in Device Manager. Nothing is uninstalled.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Device Manager".
2. Find the device VTDiag named in your report (open the group it belongs to).
3. Right-click it, choose "Disable device" and click "Yes" (do not choose "Uninstall device").
4. To undo, right-click the same device and choose "Enable device".

**Undo:** Press Undo and the device turns back on.

## Stop this program from starting with Windows

`fix.generic.disable_startup_hkcu`

This program starts every time you sign in and can clash with VALORANT. We'll switch off its auto-start; it stays installed and you can still open it yourself.

1. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager.
2. On Windows 11 open "Startup apps"; on Windows 10 open the "Startup" tab.
3. Right-click the program VTDiag named in your report and choose "Disable".
4. Restart the PC; you can still open the program yourself when you need it.

**Undo:** Press Undo and it starts with Windows again.

## Stop this program from starting with Windows (all users)

`fix.generic.disable_startup_hklm`

This program starts for every user when Windows starts and can clash with VALORANT. We'll switch off its auto-start; it stays installed.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager.
2. On Windows 11 open "Startup apps"; on Windows 10 open the "Startup" tab.
3. Right-click the program VTDiag named in your report and choose "Disable" (say "Yes" if Windows asks for admin rights).
4. Restart the PC; the program stays installed and you can still open it yourself.

**Undo:** Press Undo and it starts with Windows again.

## Remove old compatibility settings from a program

`fix.generic.remove_compat_layer`

A program has old Windows compatibility settings (like 'run in Windows 8 mode'). These can stop VALORANT or the Riot Client from starting. We'll remove the listed settings.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Close VALORANT and the Riot Client.
2. Open the folder of the program file VTDiag named in your report.
3. Right-click the file, choose "Properties" and open the "Compatibility" tab.
4. Untick only the settings listed in your report (for example "Run this program in compatibility mode for").
5. Click "OK", then start the Riot Client again.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the settings come back.

## Turn off IPv6 on this adapter

`fix.generic.unbind_ipv6`

We'll switch IPv6 off on this one network adapter. Internet keeps working over IPv4.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "ncpa.cpl" and press Enter to open Network Connections.
2. Right-click the adapter VTDiag named in your report and choose "Properties".
3. Untick "Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6)" and click "OK".
4. To undo, tick the same box again.

**Undo:** Press Undo and IPv6 is switched back on.

## Turn off mouse acceleration

`fix.input.mouse_accel_off`

'Enhance pointer precision' makes the cursor move further when you move the mouse fast. In a shooter that makes aim feel floaty and inconsistent. We'll switch it off.

**Restart needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "main.cpl" and press Enter to open Mouse Properties.
2. Open the "Pointer Options" tab.
3. Untick "Enhance pointer precision" and click "OK".
4. Restart the PC, then check your aim in the Range.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the old mouse setting comes back.

## Turn off the second network connection

`fix.net.disable_second_adapter`

Two network connections are active at the same time (for example cable and Wi-Fi). Windows can switch between them in the middle of a match, which causes lag and disconnects. We'll switch off the one you're not using.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Device Manager".
2. Open "Network adapters" and find the adapter VTDiag named in your report.
3. Right-click it, choose "Disable device" and click "Yes".
4. Check that your internet still works; to undo, right-click it and choose "Enable device".

**Undo:** Press Undo in VTDiag's undo list and the adapter turns back on.

## Turn off the network port you're not using

`fix.net.disable_unused_adapter`

Your PC has a wired Realtek network port that is switched on but not used. Its driver is known to cause short freezes every few seconds in VALORANT. We'll switch it off; your current connection keeps working.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Device Manager".
2. Open "Network adapters" and find the Realtek adapter VTDiag named in your report.
3. Right-click it, choose "Disable device" and click "Yes".
4. Check that your internet still works; to undo, right-click it and choose "Enable device".

**Undo:** Open VTDiag's undo list and press Undo. The port turns back on right away.

## Clear the DNS cache

`fix.net.dns_flush`

Windows keeps a list of internet addresses it looked up before. If an entry is old or wrong, Riot servers can't be reached. Clearing it is harmless; Windows rebuilds the list by itself.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Terminal (Admin)" (on Windows 10: "Windows PowerShell (Admin)").
2. Type "ipconfig /flushdns" and press Enter.
3. Wait for the message that the DNS cache was flushed, then start the Riot Client.

**Undo:** There is nothing to undo: Windows refills the list automatically.

## Turn off power saving on your network card

`fix.net.realtek_power_saving_off`

Your network card has 'Energy Efficient Ethernet' or 'Green Ethernet' switched on. These power-saving features can make the connection pause for a split second. We'll switch them off.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Device Manager".
2. Open "Network adapters", right-click the adapter VTDiag named in your report and choose "Properties".
3. Open the "Advanced" tab.
4. Set each of these to "Disabled" if you see it: "Energy-Efficient Ethernet", "Green Ethernet", "Advanced EEE", "Gigabit Lite".
5. Click "OK"; your connection may drop for a few seconds and then come back.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the old power-saving settings come back.

## Turn off IPv6 on your connection

`fix.net.unbind_ipv6_active`

Some network cards (for example Killer) and some internet providers have trouble with IPv6, which can break voice chat or cause VAL 57 / 59 errors. We'll switch IPv6 off only on the connection you use. Normal internet keeps working over IPv4.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "ncpa.cpl" and press Enter to open Network Connections.
2. Right-click the connection you use (the one VTDiag named in your report) and choose "Properties".
3. Untick "Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6)" and click "OK".
4. Play one match with voice chat; to undo, tick the same box again.

**Undo:** Press Undo and IPv6 is switched back on.

## Reset the Windows network settings (Winsock)

`fix.net.winsock_reset`

Extra network filters from VPNs, boosters or old software can break how Windows talks to Riot. A Winsock reset puts the network settings back to factory state. This can't be undone with a click and needs a restart.

**Admin rights needed** · **Restart needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Terminal (Admin)" (on Windows 10: "Windows PowerShell (Admin)").
2. Type "netsh winsock reset" and press Enter.
3. Restart the PC when it says so.
4. If a VPN or network tool stops working afterwards, reinstall it.

**Undo:** This can't be undone with one click. If something stops working, reinstall the VPN or network tool that needed the old settings.

## Turn off Fast Startup

`fix.os.fast_startup_off`

With Fast Startup on, 'Shut down' doesn't fully restart Windows, so Vanguard can't load fresh and old boot files stay around. We'll switch Fast Startup off so every shutdown is a clean start.

**Admin rights needed** · **Restart needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "powercfg.cpl" and press Enter to open Power Options.
2. Click "Choose what the power buttons do" on the left.
3. Click "Change settings that are currently unavailable".
4. Untick "Turn on fast startup (recommended)" and click "Save changes".
5. Restart the PC once.

**Undo:** Press Undo and Fast Startup is switched back on.

## Fix your PC clock

`fix.os.time_resync`

Your PC clock is off. A wrong clock breaks secure connections, so the Riot Client can't log in or Vanguard can't connect. We'll sync the clock with Microsoft's time server.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Open Settings > Time & language > Date & time.
2. Make sure "Set time automatically" is on, then click "Sync now".
3. Or open "Terminal (Admin)" and type "w32tm /resync", then press Enter.
4. Check that the clock is right, then start the Riot Client.

**Undo:** Undo doesn't set the clock back to the wrong time (that would break things again).

## Let the processor run at full speed

`fix.power.cpu_max_100`

The 'maximum processor state' power setting is below 100%, so your processor never reaches full speed. We'll set it back to 100%.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "powercfg.cpl" and press Enter to open Power Options.
2. Next to the plan you use, click "Change plan settings", then "Change advanced power settings".
3. Open "Processor power management" > "Maximum processor state".
4. Set "Plugged in" (or "Setting" on desktops) to 100% and click "OK".

**Undo:** Press Undo and the old limit comes back.

## Switch to the High performance power plan

`fix.power.high_performance`

Your PC uses a power plan that saves energy by slowing the processor down. We'll switch to the High performance plan so VALORANT gets full speed.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Right-click the Start button and open "Terminal (Admin)" (on Windows 10: "Windows PowerShell (Admin)").
2. Type "powercfg /setactive 8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c" and press Enter.
3. Press Win+R, type "powercfg.cpl" and check that "High performance" is now selected.
4. To undo, pick your old plan in the same window.

**Undo:** Press Undo and your old power plan comes back.

## Stop Windows from putting USB ports to sleep

`fix.power.usb_selective_suspend_off`

Windows can put USB ports to sleep to save power. On some PCs this makes the mouse, keyboard or headset drop out for a moment, or freezes the whole PC. We'll switch that off.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "powercfg.cpl" and press Enter to open Power Options.
2. Next to the plan you use, click "Change plan settings", then "Change advanced power settings".
3. Open "USB settings" > "USB selective suspend setting".
4. Set it to "Disabled" (both "On battery" and "Plugged in" if you see two) and click "OK".

**Undo:** Press Undo and the old power setting comes back.

## Close overlay and recording programs for this session

`fix.proc.close_overlays`

Overlay programs (like RivaTuner, Overwolf or clip recorders) hook into the game to draw on screen. After recent VALORANT updates, these hooks cause stutter, freezes and stuck loading. We'll close them for now; they'll start again next time you turn on your PC.

1. Find each overlay or recording program VTDiag named in your report.
2. Close its window with the X button.
3. If it still runs near the clock, right-click its tray icon and choose "Exit" or "Quit".
4. Start VALORANT and play one match; the programs start again next time you turn on your PC.

**Undo:** Nothing to undo: open the programs again whenever you want.

## Always run the Riot Client as administrator

`fix.riot.client_runasadmin`

Many players fixed freezes and black screens after updates by running the Riot Client (RiotClientServices.exe) as administrator. We'll set that option on the Riot Client only, not on the game.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Close VALORANT and the Riot Client.
2. Open the folder of RiotClientServices.exe that VTDiag named in your report.
3. Right-click RiotClientServices.exe, choose "Properties" and open the "Compatibility" tab.
4. Tick "Run this program as an administrator" and click "OK" (do not use "Change settings for all users").
5. Start the Riot Client again and say "Yes" when Windows asks.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the option is removed.

## Remove forced CPU priority from Riot programs

`fix.sec.remove_riot_perfoptions`

VALORANT or Vanguard is forced to run at 'High' or 'Realtime' priority. That starves Vanguard and Windows and can cause VAN 136 / VAN 185 kicks. We'll remove the forced priority so Windows manages it normally.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "regedit" and press Enter to open Registry Editor.
2. Go to "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\" plus the program name VTDiag named, then "PerfOptions".
3. Right-click the "PerfOptions" key and choose "Export" to save a backup.
4. In the right side, delete only the values "CpuPriorityClass" and "IoPriority" (keep the key itself).
5. Do the same for each program in the report, then restart the PC.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the forced priority comes back.

## Remove Exploit Protection overrides from Riot programs

`fix.sec.reset_exploit_overrides`

Someone (or a tweak tool) turned off Windows Exploit Protection settings for Riot or Vanguard programs. Vanguard needs those protections and shows VAN 9002 without them. We'll remove the overrides so Windows defaults apply again.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Open Windows Security > App & browser control > Exploit protection settings.
2. Open the "Program settings" tab.
3. Click the program VTDiag named in your report (for example vgc.exe) and click "Remove".
4. Do the same for each program in the report, then restart the PC.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the old overrides come back.

## Turn off the program that clashes with VALORANT

`fix.svc.disable_conflict_service`

A background program on your PC is known to clash with VALORANT or Vanguard. We'll stop it and keep it from starting with Windows. The program stays installed.

**Admin rights needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "services.msc" and press Enter to open Services.
2. Double-click the service VTDiag named in your report (check that "Service name" matches).
3. Set "Startup type" to "Disabled" and click "Apply".
4. Click "Stop", then "OK".
5. To undo, set "Startup type" back to what it was before.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the program starts with Windows again.

## Reset Vanguard's boot status file

`fix.vg.quarantine_bootstatus`

Vanguard keeps a small file (vgkbootstatus.dat) that remembers whether it started correctly. If that file is stuck, Vanguard keeps asking for a restart. We'll move it to VTDiag's quarantine folder. Then you restart.

**Admin rights needed** · **Restart needed**

1. Close VALORANT and the Riot Client, including its icon near the clock.
2. Make a new folder on your Desktop, for example "Vanguard backup".
3. Open the folder where VTDiag found vgkbootstatus.dat (the path is in your report).
4. Move the file into your Desktop folder with Cut and Paste, and click "Continue" if Windows asks (do not delete it).
5. Restart the PC, then start VALORANT.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the file is put back.

## Move an old Vanguard boot file out of the way

`fix.vg.quarantine_stale_dat`

An old Vanguard boot file (392667600.dat) was left behind, which can cause blue screens or 'restart required' loops. We'll move it to VTDiag's safe quarantine folder (not delete it). Then you restart.

**Admin rights needed** · **Restart needed**

1. Close VALORANT and the Riot Client, including its icon near the clock.
2. Make a new folder on your Desktop, for example "Vanguard backup".
3. Open the folder where VTDiag found 392667600.dat (the path is in your report).
4. Move the file into your Desktop folder with Cut and Paste, and click "Continue" if Windows asks (do not delete it).
5. Restart the PC, then start VALORANT.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the file is put back where it was.

## Make Vanguard start with Windows

`fix.vg.vgc_automatic`

Vanguard's service (vgc) is set to start only when asked, and it isn't starting properly on your PC. Riot's own fix is to set it to start automatically. We only offer this because you told us Vanguard Pre-Check is off.

**Admin rights needed** · **Restart needed**

1. Press Win+R, type "services.msc" and press Enter to open Services.
2. Double-click "vgc".
3. Set "Startup type" to "Automatic" and click "Apply".
4. Click "Start", then "OK".
5. Restart the PC, then start VALORANT.

**Undo:** Press Undo and the service goes back to its old start setting.
